source.title: Dissociable Learning Processes Underlie Human Pain Conditioning

confidence_rationale: Human pain conditioning with model-based fMRI: learned associability and PE of a non-specific preparatory system correlate with amygdala-striatal responses; a second, response-specific (lateralised limb withdrawal) system's associability correlates with ipsilateral cerebellum. Supports aversive associability as a learning-rate state and adds that associability is carried separately per learning system. Correlational.
failure_signatures: Two dissociable aversive learning systems each carried their own associability; a single associability vector per cue shared by all consumers would not reproduce the preparatory/consummatory split.
The response-specific associability localised to cerebellum, not amygdala, so aversive associability is not uniquely amygdalar.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In human Pavlovian pain conditioning, a non-specific preparatory system (autonomic, facial) and a specific lateralised consummatory system (limb withdrawal) are learned by dissociable reinforcement-learning processes; the preparatory system's associability and PE correlate with amygdala-striatal fMRI responses, the consummatory system's associability with ipsilateral cerebellar cortex.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-598's core in the most REE-relevant aversive modality (pain). The two-system split also lines up with SD-011's affective (z_harm_a) vs sensory-discriminative (z_harm_s) streams: an associability state may be needed per stream, not once per cue. That refines the V3 design space (one associability vector per consumer).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Model-based correlations. The eligibility window here is a single cue per trial, not a retrospective window over candidate causes. Mapping the preparatory/consummatory split onto SD-011's streams is my interpretation, not the paper's.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI with EMG and SCR, probabilistic thermal pain to left/right arm predicted by visual cues, RL modelling

confidence_components.notes: Current Biology, careful modelling, human pain. Mapping good for aversive associability; the two-system result is a bonus constraint.
